cards.title: What is JSX?
cards.content:
JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It is a syntax extension for JavaScript that allows us to write HTML-like code inside JavaScript.

const element = <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;

options.text: JSX is executed directly by the browser without any compilation.
JSX is a syntax extension that gets compiled to standard JavaScript function calls.
JSX is a completely new programming language replacing JavaScript.

cards.title: Embedding Expressions in JSX
cards.content:
You can put any valid JavaScript expression inside curly braces {} within JSX.

const name = 'React';
const element = <h1>Hello, {name}</h1>;

content.text: To embed JavaScript expressions in JSX, we wrap the expression in curly ____.

cards.title: Rules of JSX
cards.content:
• Must return a single root element (or use fragments <></>).
  • All tags must be closed.
  • Use camelCase for most property names (e.g., className instead of class).
